The distillation process is further refined through a dual-head adversarial scheme, which decouples the discrimination of spatial details and temporal consistency into two separate heads operating in both the pixel space and the feature space of a VAE decoder. This approach aims to balance the optimization of both spatial detail richness and temporal coherence, preventing the student model from producing either over-smoothed outputs or flickering results. The authors demonstrate through extensive experiments that their proposed AdcVSR model achieves a significant reduction in model complexity, with a 95% parameter reduction and an 8x acceleration in inference speed compared to its DOVE teacher. Despite this substantial efficiency gain, the proposed model maintains competitive video quality, as evidenced by quantitative metrics and qualitative assessments. The paper's primary contribution lies in its novel ADC method, which effectively compresses a large Real-VSR model into an efficient diffusion-GAN hybrid, and the architectural innovation of the 2D + 1D design, which achieves a favorable balance between performance and computational cost.
